newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila set to relax farm commodities imports.
newsitem.headline: Manila set to relax farm commodities imports.

text.p: The Philippines, faced with U.S. warnings of trade sanctions for failing to meet commitments on frozen pork imports last year, plans to relax rules on local importers of agricultural products, a senior official said.

Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said his department was waiting for the opinion of the Justice Department on whether or not it can issue the new rules because of a Manila court order stopping imports of agricultural products at lower tariff rates.
Present government rules limit the volume of imports of corn, sugar, frozen pork, beef and chicken that private firms can bring into the country at lower tariffs.
Licensing of firms joining the government's minimum access volume (MAV) programme is also limited to those which have been traditionally importing such products.
Last month, a Manila court stopped the government's MAV programme upon petition by the Philippine Federation of Food Industries Inc which represents traders and commodities importers.
The group protested that the benefits of lower tariffs were available only to existing players.

Early this year, the United States also threatened to ask the World Trade Organisation to take disciplinary action against the Philippines unless Manila fulfilled its commitment to import pork from U.S. producers.
U.S. meat producers had complained the Philippines was blocking fair market access for their pork. Escudero denied the charge.
Manila allowed imports of up to 49,000 tonnes of frozen pork under the MAV programme in 1996 but Philippine meat processors imported only 2,500 tonnes.
Escudero said imports were low because Filipinos did not like the taste of frozen pork.
